results.hypothesis_statement: In a synthetic parametric trend-following process with persistent returns, increasing the strategy’s lookback window will improve risk-adjusted out-of-sample performance up to a finite range, after which performance will deteriorate because signal responsiveness becomes insufficient to capture regime changes.

parsed.hypothesis_statement: In a synthetic parametric trend-following process with persistent returns, increasing the strategy’s lookback window will improve risk-adjusted out-of-sample performance up to a finite range, after which performance will deteriorate because signal responsiveness becomes insufficient to capture regime changes.
parsed.hypothesis_rationale: The lookback window controls a bias–variance and responsiveness trade-off: short windows produce noisy estimates of the latent trend, whereas long windows smooth noise but lag changes in the trend regime. A parameterized synthetic generator with explicitly varied persistence and regime-switching behavior permits this proposed non-monotonic relationship to be falsified across controlled scenarios.

requirements.label: Generate reproducible synthetic price/return paths across persistence, noise, and regime-switching parameter settings.
Evaluate fixed strategy logic over a prespecified grid of lookback windows using separated in-sample and out-of-sample path segments.
Estimate the relationship between lookback length and out-of-sample risk-adjusted performance, including uncertainty across simulation seeds and generator settings.
